articles.summary: Alex Eala advances to the second round of the US Open for the second straight year as she ends the dream run of American qualifier Mary Stoiana

blocks.text: GRATEFUL. The Philippines' Alexandra Eala celebrates winning her first-round match against against Mary Stoiana of the United States in the 2026 US Open.
Geoff Burke/IMAGN IMAGES/Reuters
Alex Eala advances to the second round of the US Open for the second straight year as she ends the dream run of American qualifier Mary Stoiana

items: Alex Eala had a strong start at the US Open, defeating American qualifier Mary Stoiana 6-1, 6-2 in the first round.
Eala, the 17th seed, advanced to the second round for the second consecutive year and will face Ukraine's Oleksandra Oliynykova next.
The match marked Eala's fewest dropped games since Wimbledon, and she aims to improve on her previous US Open performance.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Alex Eala could not have had a better start to her US Open campaign.

The Filipina ace demolished American qualifier Mary Stoiana in the opening round, coasting to a 6-1, 6-2 win before an adoring crowd at the Louis Armstrong Stadium in Flushing Meadows, New York, on Tuesday, September 1 (Wednesday, September 2, Manila time).

Living up to her billing as the 17th seed, Eala swatted aside an untested Stoiana, who made her Grand Slam main draw debut, as she advanced to the second round of the US Open for the second straight year.
Eala won the first five games to clinch the opening set in just 31 minutes before Stoiana, ranked 122nd in the world, showed some resistance by taking a 2-1 lead in the second set.

But that only delayed what seemed like an inevitability as Eala reeled off four consecutive games to wrap up the match in 1 hour and 18 minutes and arrange a round-of-64 clash with Ukraine’s Oleksandra Oliynykova.

“Of course, it was very difficult. Every exchange had its own challenges, especially in the start of the second set. I think she put me in uncomfortable positions,” said Eala. “I’m really happy with this match.”
Eala ended what had been a dream US Open run for Stoiana, who won three matches in qualifying to reach a Grand Slam main draw for the first time in her career.

The win marked the fewest games Eala dropped since she beat Mexico’s Renata Zarazua by the same score in the opening round of the recent Wimbledon Championships, where she made it as far as the fourth round.
Eala hopes to replicate her Wimbledon exploits as she targets a deeper US Open run, a year after Spain’s Cristina Bucsa ousted her in the second round.
She can surpass her 2025 showing by getting back at world No. 46 Oliynykova, who scored a 6-4, 6-4 win over USA’s Reese Brantmeier in their second-round clash.
A win over Oliynykova will allow Eala to level their head-to-head record on the WTA Tour after the Ukrainian beat her in three sets in the Strasbourg Open in France in May. – Rappler.com

articles.title: US urges hands-off approach to AI regulation at G20 tech meeting
articles.summary: The US goals largely align with the thinking of the world's biggest AI companies. They want less regulation around the world for their rapidly growing businesses, or to shape the rules as they are…

blocks.text: G20 MEETING. White House science and technology advisor Michael Kratsios speaks to delegates at the G20 Innovation Ministerial summit, in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA, September 1, 2026.
Jonathan Drake/Reuters

The US goals largely align with the thinking of the world's biggest AI companies. They want less regulation around the world for their rapidly growing businesses, or to shape the rules as they are written.

items: The US urged G20 members to avoid strict AI regulations, aligning with major American AI companies seeking less oversight.
US tech adviser Michael Kratsios promoted the 'Carolina Principles' for AI regulation, which China has signed, focusing on rules for novel situations rather than new regulations.
The meeting highlighted concerns over China's advancing AI capabilities and the need for the US to maintain its technological leadership amid growing competition.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

NORTH CAROLINA, USA – The US pressed G20 members on Tuesday, September 1, to take a hands-off approach to AI regulation and avoid creating rules for the technology at a gathering of industry titans and commerce ministers in North Carolina.

The US goals largely align with the thinking of the world’s biggest AI companies, nearly all of which are American. They want less regulation around the world for their rapidly growing businesses, or to shape the rules as they are written. Federal government requirements could hurt the industry’s profits if they slow the release of new models or ​prompt the companies to change how their ​products perform to address security concerns.

US tech adviser Michael Kratsios, who is co-hosting the two-day meeting, advocated for countries to adopt the “Carolina Principles.” Countries that signed on agreed to avoid writing entirely new regulations for AI, and instead focus on writing rules for “novel” situations involving the technology, he told the G20 officials in a speech on Tuesday morning.

The Chinese government signed the principles, he told reporters on Tuesday afternoon. He did not provide a copy of the document. The Chinese embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

“Policymakers do not need to approach each innovation in isolation and should not treat every emerging technology as a first-of-its-kind policy problem,” Kratsios said in his morning speech to the delegates.
China’s Technology and Science Minister Yin Hejun represented the Chinese Communist Party at the gathering. Kratsios told reporters he had a “great” bilateral meeting with his Chinese counterpart.
Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown is slated to address the group on Wednesday, a company spokesperson said.
Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk addressed the gathering by video on Tuesday.
Hassabis called on the G20 officials to set up safety tests for AI systems.

Zuckerberg said countries should not restrict open-weight AI models. Open-weight AI models are systems with publicly accessible core elements. Zuckerberg has tried in recent weeks to position his company as a leader in open-weight models, and restrictions could dampen his ambitions.

Musk criticized the European Union’s tech regulations, saying that the EU’s policy “inhibits progress” for companies. He also urged leaders outside China to develop new energy sources to power data centers. Debates over data centers have become a key political issue in the U.S. ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, with development influencing voter attitudes toward candidates.

A United Nations panel recently warned that AI’s developments are outpacing scientific understanding and government policy. Recent events, including a hack triggered by a rogue OpenAI agent that compromised the infrastructure of AI company Hugging Face, added to concerns about how closely leading AI companies are monitoring tests of their products. AI agents are programs that run with minimal human supervision.
The G20 leaders are convening at a key moment in the AI sector’s development and the global debate over how to govern it, and as the US faces an increasing threat from China for AI supremacy.

Chinese open-weight AI models are becoming increasingly capable when compared to proprietary systems from American AI giants such as Anthropic and OpenAI. Chinese-made open-weight models are gaining ground with US companies, also posing a potential security risk if the country’s leaders decide to interfere.

“It has increased urgency for this administration to make sure that the rest of the world stays within the American tech ecosystem and doesn’t seek alternatives,” said Vivek Chilukuri, a technology and national security fellow at the Center for a New American Security.
The ​meeting is one of a series of gatherings taking ​place ⁠over the next few months in US cities leading up to the G20 leaders’ summit in Miami in December.
Reuters previously reported that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will separately appear before the delegates with Howard Lutnick, the US commerce secretary, on Wednesday.

A handful of protesters gathered outside the G20 meeting. John Montavon, a protester from North Carolina, disagreed with Musk’s advocacy for data centers, adding that their power needs would make the planet warmer.
“Mr. Musk has shown he is completely disassociated from the reality that most of us live in,” he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Tunisia's human rights defenders decry civil society crackdown
articles.summary: Five years into the authoritarian rule of Tunisian President Kais Saied, Human Rights Watch and other activists warn that Tunisia's once vibrant civil society is in danger of being completely stifled.

image.caption: Tunisians have been protesting against President Kais Saied this summer, demanding the restoration of democracy and calling for the release of jailed activists and journalists amid a worsening economic and social crisisImage: Jihed Abidellaoui/REUTERS

blocks.text: "Most civil society organizations are in a state of shock today," Messaoud Romdhani, a Tunisian human rights activist told DW. "Those who criticize the authorities or situation in Tunisia face widespread repression," he explained, adding that "most have been accused of money laundering, which leads to the suspension of their activities."
Another Tunisian activist, who spoke with DW on condition of anonymity, also said that increasingly people were thinking twice before speaking in public or even choosing to work on sensitive issues.
"What worries me most is the chilling effect: When organizations face suspension and activists face prosecution or detention, the uncertainty itself becomes a form of pressure," he said.

Human Rights Watch has also raised the alarm. In its latest report, published Wednesday morning, the international rights watchdog concludes that Saied is attempting to shutter Tunisia's civil society entirely.

"It is clear that the authorities are abusing every tool at their disposal to close the space for civil society in Tunisia," the report reads. The watchdog also points out that civil society groups in Tunisia have played a key role in holding power to account, delivering essential services and advocating for people's human rights.

"The government has used abusive, arbitrary prosecutions, detentions, financial investigations and suspension of organizations in an attempt to stifle these voices," Bassam Khawaja, a deputy director in the Middle East and North Africa Division at Human Rights Watch and editor of the report, told DW.
He added that it was clear the idea was to shut down all opposition and independent voices in the country. "This amounts to a total crackdown on civil society in Tunisia," he said.

blocks.caption: Young Tunisians are increasingly unhappy with the government, while older Tunisians are more satisfied that a decade ago, according to one surveyImage: Jihed Abidellaoui/REUTERS

blocks.text: Saied was elected president democratically in 2019. But in July 2021, he dissolved parliament and launched a power grab. Since then, he has dismantled most democratic bodies, repressed political dissent and arrested opposition figures.

For Anthony Dworkin, a senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations who focuses on human rights and democracy, Saied's goals remain unchanged. "They have been the same for the last five years, namely to consolidate power and remove potential checks on and critics of his rule," he told DW.

Saied has rejected accusations that he is an authoritarian ruler and argued that his measures are necessary to tackle corruption and uphold democracy. He has accused critics of receiving foreign funding to stir unrest and undermine Tunisia's national interests. DW reached out to the Tunisian presidency for comment but had not received a response by the time of publication.
Growing discontent prompts calls for Saied's resignation

Despite the widespread crackdown on dissent, some people still dare criticize the government. On July 25, the fifth anniversary of the president's power grab, thousands took to the streets of the capital, Tunis, to protest worsening living conditions, democratic backsliding and the government's handling of basic services.

The demonstrations came amid widespread water and electricity outages, which Saied has described as "premeditated acts aimed at inflaming the situation by all means and spreading lies and rumors to sow confusion."
In late August, protesters once again called on the president to step down by chanting "The people want the fall of the regime," a popular slogan from the 2010-2011 Arab Spring uprising.

The demonstration was initiated by Nafas, a new citizen-led umbrella initiative that was launched in May. Mohamed Hawel, a university teacher and member of the Nafas collective, told the news agency AP that Nafas was created to unite people around basic necessities, including water, electricity and food.
Growing gap between older, younger Tunisians

Despite some unity at these protests, according to an Arab Barometersurvey there is an emerging generational divide in Tunisia. A report published in July on the basis of a survey conducted in the fall of 2025 found that older and less educated people had vastly different views on the country's economic and political conditions from younger, better educated people.

The survey showed that the older generation saw the current political and economic situation in the most positive light since the Arab Spring and had more trust in the government than over the past decade.

In comparison, younger Tunisians were more pessimistic about the country's economic and political development. They also remained more skeptical of state institutions while maintaining a high trust in civil society organizations: 49% of people between the ages of 18-39 expressed trust in these, compared with only 32% of those aged 40 and older.

"What really stands out in Tunisia is that the recent decline in trust in civil society is almost entirely a story about older Tunisians. Two years prior, there was almost no generational gap between citizens," Michael Robbins, the director of Arab Barometer, told DW. "Since then, trust in civil society among Tunisians 40 and older has fallen quite sharply, while it has not changed meaningfully among those who are aged 18-39."
Tunisia has a population of approximately 12 million people. People aged 18–39 account for roughly 30% of the population, while those aged 40 and older account for approximately 43%.

"I think the notion of a divided society is overstated," said Dworkin. "Moreover, the recent demonstrations are not large enough to pose a serious threat to Kais Saied," he added, while admitting that Saied had lost considerable public support over his failure to improve the country's economy. "But there are no attractive political alternatives and people are also tired of political upheaval."
In his view, many Tunisians are just trying to get by with daily life, while many others are looking to emigrate.
DW's Tarek Guizani in Tunis contributed to this report.

articles.title: DOH has enough leptospirosis medicines, Mercado says
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Acting Health Secretary Edwin Mercado said on Wednesday that the agency has sufficient stocks of leptospirosis medicine to meet demand, if needed, to address the flood-borne…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Acting Health Secretary Edwin Mercado said on Wednesday that the agency has sufficient stocks of leptospirosis medicine to meet demand, if needed, to address the flood-borne illness.
At a congressional budget hearing, Mercado said the Department of Health (DOH) has around 3.1 million pills stored at its main warehouse that could be distributed to flooded communities.
“We have at least 3.1 million capsules still in the central warehouse, which is enough buffer for the rest of the year,” he told lawmakers.

He did not specify the medicine he was referring to, although he responded to a question asked by 4K Partylist Rep. Iris Montes, who asked if the DOH had procured “prophylaxis” treatment for leptospirosis.

Post‑exposure treatment for those who wade through floodwaters involves doxycycline, a pill now under scrutiny amid supply concerns after torrential rains brought by monsoon rains left several areas flooded.

In mid-August, the University of Santo Tomas Hospital disputed reports that its doxycycline supply was depleted. Last week, Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko” Moreno Domagoso said the capital still has sufficient stocks of the pill despite heavy rains that inundated the flood-prone city.
The DOH plans to procure 4.88 million doxycycline pills for next year, which will be distributed to health centers nationwide, Mercado said. /jpv

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial: Who is Michael Poa?
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Michael Poa, one of Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense lawyers for her impeachment trial, takes the stand as one of the prosecution’s hostile witnesses as the Senate…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Michael Poa, one of Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense lawyers for her impeachment trial, takes the stand as one of the prosecution’s hostile witnesses as the Senate impeachment court tackles Duterte’s alleged misuse of the Department of Education’s (DepEd) confidential funds.
Poa, a partner at the Poa Himala & Virtucio Law Offices, was admitted to the bar in 2019 after earning his Bachelor of Laws at the University of the Philippines.
He also has a bachelor’s degree in Creative Arts and Italian Studies from Flinders University.
But despite being a lawyer, Poa is most known for serving the government in various capacities under Duterte.
From July 2022 to 2023, Poa served as the DepEd Action Center’s spokesperson, before being promoted to undersecretary from 2023 to July 2024.
He then assumed the role of being the DepEd’s main mouthpiece from August to November 2024.
His brief stint as the DepEd’s spokesperson ended after he resigned from the department—alongside Duterte who left her post as education secretary.
Immediately after this, he was named the spokesperson of the Office of the Vice President. This was his last known position in the government.
Outside of his roles in the government, Poa is also known for handling criminal, civil and commercial litigation, taxation, as well as special projects. /jpv

articles.title: Nepal seeks urgent climate finance after Bhotekoshi flood
articles.summary: The government has sent an urgent request to the board of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, a global climate finance mechanism, seeking financial assistance for Nepal following the deadly…

blocks.text: The government has sent an urgent request to the board of the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage, a global climate finance mechanism, seeking financial assistance for Nepal following the deadly Bhotekoshi flood of August 26.

The mechanism was established at COP27 in 2022 and operationalised at COP28. A letter cosigned by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Forests and Agriculture Minister Geeta Chaudhary, a copy of which has been seen by the Post, seeks an immediate response to the catastrophic flash flood.

“We write to draw your urgent attention to the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Bhotekoshi river basin, causing widespread loss of life, displacement, destruction of homes and critical infrastructure, and severe disruption to essential services, livelihoods, markets, and connectivity across downstream communities,” the letter reads.

Maheshwar Dhakal, joint secretary at the Ministry of Forests and a member of the fund’s board, told the Post that the letter does not specify the actual scale of the losses and that it is up to the board to decide on financial assistance.
“Almost all major donors and global development partners are members of the board, and Nepal’s claims and potential risks are well-established, so the board must compensate us,” he said.

The disaster has affected a fragile transboundary mountain river system and generated cascading consequences extending far beyond the immediate flood zone, according to the letter. Search, rescue, relief and rapid damage-assessment operations are continuing, it says.

“The full scale of economic and non-economic loss and damage has yet to be determined; however, preliminary information indicates that the consequences are extensive and exceed Nepal’s immediate response capacity,” the letter reads.

If Nepal is able to secure support from the fund, it would set an example for other vulnerable countries, Dhakal said. The scale of damage caused by the flood, and the search, rescue, relief, rehabilitation and reconstruction required in its aftermath, has become a major challenge for Nepal, he said.

“Since we are genuinely suffering from the adverse effects of climate change, we have approached the board. The next board meeting is expected to convene on December 10, but we want to get an immediate response and support before that,” he told the Post, noting that this is the first time Nepal has sought support from the entity.

As a least developed and highly climate-vulnerable mountainous country, Nepal contributes negligibly to global greenhouse gas emissions yet continues to bear disproportionate and escalating climate impacts, the letter says.

It adds that the Bhotekoshi disaster demonstrates how extreme events in the cryosphere can rapidly cascade from high mountains to densely populated downstream areas, undermining development gains and affecting water, food, energy, health, infrastructure, ecosystems and human security.

“In view of the exceptional urgency and magnitude of this disaster, the Government of Nepal respectfully requests the Board to take a special decision to respond rapidly, directly, and effectively in accordance with its Governing Instrument,” the letter says.

“Time is of the essence,” it adds. “A prompt response would help protect affected populations, restore essential services, prevent further suffering and demonstrate that the fund can translate international solidarity into timely support for vulnerable countries and communities when it is most urgently needed.”

During an interview with Kantipur Television on Monday, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said Nepal would raise the flood and its impacts with the international community. He said a letter had already been sent to the board on Monday through the Ministry of Finance.

In December 2024, Nepal drew the attention of the International Court of Justice to the impacts of climate change, making a strong plea for climate justice to alleviate the suffering of Nepali citizens.

Making a presentation to the court’s public hearings on the “Obligations of States in respect of Climate Change”, then Foreign Minister Arzu Rana Deuba said global warming and consequent climate change increasingly threaten Nepal’s snow-capped mountains and glaciers. /dl

articles.title: Haze blankets parts of Occidental Mindoro
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — A thick haze has been observed in parts of Occidental Mindoro, including Calintaan town, as smoke from forest and land fires in Indonesia reached several areas of the…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — A thick haze has been observed in parts of Occidental Mindoro, including Calintaan town, as smoke from forest and land fires in Indonesia reached several areas of the Philippines, local disaster officials said.

The Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) of Rizal town in Occidental Mindoro warned residents about the haze after reports indicated that the southwest monsoon has carried smoke from fires in Indonesian districts of Sumatra and Kalimantan toward Southeast Asia.
Photos released by the Provincial Information Office of Occidental Mindoro on Wednesday showed murky aerial conditions in Calintaan.
According to the MDRRMO, moderate to heavy haze was headed for several areas of Luzon, Mimaropa, Bicol and the Visayas based on a 6 p.m. report on Aug. 31.
Areas experiencing moderate to heavy haze are Palawan, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro, Marinduque, and Romblon.
Light to moderate haze was also reported in parts of Metro Manila, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, Tarlac, Cavite, Laguna, Rizal, Batangas and Quezon.

Several provinces in Bicol and the Visayas were likewise affected, including Camarines Norte, Camarines Sur, Catanduanes, Albay, Sorsogon, Masbate, Antique, Aklan, Capiz, Iloilo, Guimaras, Negros Occidental, Negros Oriental, Cebu, Bohol, Leyte, Biliran and Samar.
The MDRRMO advised residents to limit prolonged outdoor activities while haze persists, particularly in areas where smoke is visibly thick.
Those who need to go outdoors were encouraged to wear face masks to reduce exposure to smoke and fine particulate matter.
Children, older adults and people with sensitive respiratory systems were urged to take extra precautions and remain indoors when possible.
The haze comes as parts of Southeast Asia continue to deal with smoke from forest and land fires, with wind conditions carrying the pollutants across national borders./coa

articles.title: Architect of British government’s AI strategy joins Anthropic
articles.summary:
Matt Clifford, who drafted AI action plan and advised Starmer and Sunak, hired for senior role at US firm

The architect of the UK government’s AI strategy has joined the US startup Anthropic…
articles.byline: Dan Milmo, Robert Booth and Kiran Stacey

blocks.text: The architect of the UK government’s AI strategy has joined the US startup Anthropic in a senior role a year after stepping down from his Downing Street post.
Matt Clifford, a successful tech investor, was appointed as AI opportunities adviser by Keir Starmer last year but resigned from the unpaid role six months later for personal reasons.

Clifford is moving to Anthropic as managing director, international affairs, and will lead the company’s engagement with governments outside the US including in the UK, Europe, Asia-Pacific and India.

Anthropic said Clifford would remain as chair of government-backed Aria, the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency, which funds “moonshot” science and tech projects. He will also maintain his chair role at Entrepreneurs First, the tech venture capital firm he co-founded.
A not-for-profit campaign group said the move raised questions about the “revolving door” between government and industry for former government advisers as well as ministers.

The path from elected office to Silicon Valley is already well-established after the former deputy prime minister Nick Clegg took a senior role at Meta in 2018, followed last year by the former prime minister Rishi Sunak taking advisory roles at Microsoft and Anthropic – and the ex-chancellor George Osborne joining OpenAI.
Clifford, 41, said the most important decisions about AI would be made by companies and governments “together”.
He added: “Countries everywhere want real agency over how this technology is built and used, and my job is to make Anthropic a genuine partner in that – in Europe, Asia and beyond.”
Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, is preparing for a stock exchange flotation that could value the business at $2tn (£1.5tn).
Tom Brake, the chief executive of Unlock Democracy, a not-for-profit campaign group, said the move showed “the revolving door is a problem for advisers as much as it is for ministers”.

“Taking extensive knowledge obtained within government, about a policy as sensitive as AI to a private sector company shortly after leaving government gives that company a huge advantage,” said Brake, a Liberal Democrat MP from 1997 to 2019.

Beeban Kidron, the crossbench peer and prominent critic of the government’s AI policy, said: “We need more independent politics, which puts the interests of workers, citizens and society at the forefront of our relationship with the tech sector.”

MP Chi Onwurah, Labour chair of the science, innovation and technology committee, said Clifford had made a “significant contribution” to domestic AI policy and movement between the public and private sector should be allowed.
But she said it was a matter of “some concern” that he was taking his knowledge to a global AI player so soon after leaving government.
after newsletter promotion
“I hope he will use his skills and experience to promote responsible AI to Anthropic rather than promoting irresponsible AI to the UK government,” she said.

An Anthropic spokesperson said the UK was “one of dozens” of governments Clifford’s team would engage with. “We hire people with expertise and who understand how government works because our work requires it – in every market, not just the UK.”

Prior to his government work, Clifford was already an established figure on the UK tech scene as a co-founder of Entrepreneurs First, which has helped build tech companies with a combined worth of more than $20bn.

Clifford had worked with Sunak’s government as the former prime minister’s representative to the 2023 AI Safety Summit in the UK, and helped create the organisation that later became the world-leading AI Security Institute.
He was appointed as Starmer’s AI adviser after drafting the government’s AI action plan, which supports the creation of AI growth zones to host datacentres and the building of the UK’s own AI models.
He was appointed chair of Aria in 2022. It is understood that he will step back from any matter involving Anthropic at Aria.

articles.title: USS Abraham Lincoln arrives at Thai port after gruelling 270 days at sea
articles.summary:
Ship has been plagued by reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health because of lengthy deployment

The USS Abraham Lincoln, an US aircraft carrier at the centre of a…
articles.byline: Natasha May in Pattaya, and agencies

blocks.text: The USS Abraham Lincoln, an US aircraft carrier at the centre of a row over conditions on board after months at sea as part of Donald Trump’s war against Iran, has arrived off a Thai port.

Reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health on the vessel, including attempted suicides, have made headlines around the world, provoking criticism of the president’s actions in the Middle East.

A heavy security presence was in force at Laem Chabang port near Pattaya, south of Bangkok, where the 5,000-strong crew of the USS Abraham Lincoln arrived on Wednesday morning after more than 270 days at sea.
The huge nuclear-powered ship left California in November 2025 for duty in the South China Sea and was rerouted to the Middle East before US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began six months ago.
The Lincoln left California in November 2025 for duty in the South China Sea and was rerouted to the Middle East before US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began six months ago.
The resort city of Pattaya, a rest-and-recreation destination for US troops since the Vietnam war, has stepped up security as it prepares to welcome the sailors and Marines.

blocks.caption: A tug boat greets the USS Abraham Lincoln as it arrives at the port in Laem Chabang, Chonburi, Thailand. Photograph: Sakchai Lalit/AP

blocks.text: The sailors will disembark in groups of approximately 50, according to police colonel Anek Srathongyoo, a superintendent of Pattaya city police station.

Once a quiet fishing village, Pattaya was transformed into one of the most infamous red light districts in the world with the arrival of American troops using military bases in Thailand during the Vietnam war.
At its peak, tens of thousands of US military personnel came through each year, said Pipatpong Fakfare, an associate professor specialising in tourism at Bangkok University.

“In my opinion, it’s really the founding influence for the town. The US military turned a quiet fishing village into a global destination for an international nightlife and entertainment hub in about 15 years,” he said.
Pattaya is now hugely popular with foreign tourists, known for its beaches and a nightlife scene that has long drawn scrutiny over sex tourism.

Although the American troops left by the mid-70s, the sex industry infrastructure continued to grow, with European tourists taking their place, and more recently waves of Chinese and Russian visitors, Pipatpong said.

blocks.caption: The USS Abraham Lincoln has 5,000 sailors aboard. Photograph: Anthony Wallace/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Sex work is illegal in Thailand, but authorities often turn a blind eye, said Pattarachit Gozzoli, a sociologist at Mahidol University in Bangkok.

Pattaya’s mayor, Poramase Ngampiches, has downplayed the city’s past, saying there had been a recent crackdown on sex workers but denied it was linked to the US arrivals. Local police arrested 25 women for soliciting on the beachfront promenade a week before the ship arrived.
The mayor said buses had been arranged to transport the sailors between the ship and Pattaya until the carrier departs on Sunday.
Outside one bar, a sign said: “Welcome all US military personnel. Thank you for your service.”
Poramase said in a Facebook post: “They come to relax. Our preparations will focus on safety and ensuring fair pricing, so we don’t take advantage of them.”

He said they had been banned from water sports such as jetskis, and from taking advantage of Thailand’s lax cannabis laws, but encouraged them to enjoy the city’s many other attractions, from malls to religious sites.

articles.title: 'Pilandok' moves northwest over Philippine Sea as habagat continues to dump rains
articles.summary: Tropical Storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) is moving northwestward over the Philippine Sea while the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and…

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 11:39am
Satellite rendering shows Tropical Storm Pilandok taken as of 10:40 a.m. of Sept. 2, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) is moving northwestward over the Philippine Sea while the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and the Visayas, PAGASA said Wednesday.
In its 11 a.m. bulletin on Wednesday, September 2, the state weather bureau said Pilandok was located 1,350 kilometers east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon.
Pilandok was carrying maximum sustained winds of 65 kilometers per hour near the center, with gustiness of up to 80 kph and a central pressure of 998 hPa.
It was moving northwestward at 10 kph.
Pilandok is not directly affecting the country's land areas, while the southwest monsoon continues to bring heavy rainfall and strong to gale-force winds over parts of the country.
Strong winds

PAGASA said the southwest monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over most of Luzon and Visayas, as well as Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental until Friday, September 4.
PAGASA said strong to gale-force gusts are particularly possible in coastal and upland areas exposed to the winds.
Heavy rainfall
The state weather bureau said the southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and the Visayas through Saturday, September 5.

blocks.text: PAGASA said forecast rainfall may be higher in mountainous and elevated areas. The impacts in some areas may also be worsened by significant antecedent rainfall.
Sea conditions
A gale warning is in effect over the northern and western seaboards of Northern Luzon.

Very rough seas with waves reaching up to 5 meters are expected over the seaboards of Batanes, Ilocos Norte and northern Ilocos Sur, as well as the northern and western seaboards of the Babuyan Islands.
Waves of up to 4.5 meters are also forecast over the seaboard of La Union, the western seaboard of Pangasinan, and the remaining seaboards of the Babuyan Islands and Ilocos Sur.
PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types and tonnage of vessels under these conditions.
Small seacraft operators, including those using motorbancas, are also advised not to venture out to sea in affected waters, especially if inexperienced or operating ill-equipped vessels.
Track, intensity
PAGASA said Pilandok is forecast to remain a tropical storm as it moves northwestward throughout the forecast period.
The tropical cyclone is expected to remain far from the Philippine landmass and is forecast to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility tonight, September 2, or early Thursday morning, September 3.
Pilandok has maximum sustained winds of 65 kph near the center, with gustiness of up to 80 kph. Strong to gale-force winds extend outward up to 580 kilometers from its center.
PAGASA emphasized that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still be experienced in localities outside the landfall point and forecast confidence cone.
The state weather bureau also said Pilandok's track may still shift within the limit of the forecast confidence cone.

articles.title: Free toll on Pulilan-San Fernando route starting Sept. 2
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Toll fees for all vehicles travelling between Pulilan, Bulacan, and San Fernando, Pampanga, on the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) will be waived starting Wednesday. According to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Toll fees for all vehicles travelling between Pulilan, Bulacan, and San Fernando, Pampanga, on the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) will be waived starting Wednesday.
According to the DOTr, this is in response to the heavy traffic jam affecting many motorists along portions of NLEX due to heavy flooding at Tulaoc Bridge in San Simon, Pampanga.
“Magpapatuloy ang libreng toll hanggang sa bumalik sa normal ang sitwasyon sa NLEX,” said the DOTr in a Facebook post.
(The free toll fee will continue until the situation at NLEX goes back to normal.)

The agency said Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez personally coordinated with NLEx Corporation President Luis Reñon to waive toll fees from Pulilan to San Fernando and vice versa for all vehicles.
The DOTr and the Toll Regulatory Board also directed NLEx Corporation to provide food and water, and establish portalets for motorists who will be stuck in the traffic jam.

“Nakausap ko po si NLEX President Luis Reñon para matulungan ang ating mga motorista at mga pasahero na labis na naapektuhan nitong matinding traffic, alinsunod sa utos ng ating Pangulo. Nagpapasalamat po tayo dahil agad din po silang tumugon sa ating hiling na magpatupad ng libreng toll hanggang sa maging maayos ang sitwasyon ng trapiko,” Lopez said in the same post.

(I spoke to NLEX President Luis Reñon to help our motorists and commuters affected by the heavy traffic, in line with the President’s directive. We express our gratitude for their immediate response to waive toll fees.)/coa

articles.title: Poa declared hostile witness by impeachment court
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense counsel Michael Poa was declared by the Senate impeachment court as a hostile witness at the resumption of the trial on Wednesday. Poa was…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense counsel Michael Poa was declared by the Senate impeachment court as a hostile witness at the resumption of the trial on Wednesday.
Poa was called by the prosecution panel to testify on the P112.5 million in Department of Education (DepEd) confidential funds when Duterte was its secretary.
“The chair will proceed to declare Atty. Poa as a hostile witness, therefore giving Atty. [Benjamin] Tolosa the right to ask leading questions,” presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero said.
Hostile witnesses are individuals presumed to favor the opposite party – in Poa’s case, the respondent, who is the vice president.
When Duterte was the secretary of DepEd from 2022 to 2024, Poa served as the agency’s chief of staff, an officer-in-charge of DepEd’s finance unit, and later Duterte’s spokesperson.
After Duterte’s stint at DepEd, Poa represented Duterte when she faced the first set of impeachment complaints against her in 2025.
At present, he is one of Duterte’s defense lawyers. /gsg

articles.title: One of 3 justices opposes move to drop Bonoan from plunder case
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — One of the three Sandiganbayan Fifth Division justices opposed the dropping of plunder and graft charges against former Department of Public Works (DPWH) chief Manuel Bonoan.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — One of the three Sandiganbayan Fifth Division justices opposed the dropping of plunder and graft charges against former Department of Public Works (DPWH) chief Manuel Bonoan.

Prosecutors from the Office of the Ombudsman filed on June 29, a Motion for Leave to File Amended Information to discharge Bonoan from the two cases as the anti-graft body accepted his offer to be a state witness to testify against several personalities implicated in the multibillion flood control corruption scandal.

Bonoan is a co-accused of Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, who faces a plunder case stemming from alleged “intricate mechanism involving illegal budgetary insertions and project allocations” within the DPWH infrastructure portfolio for fiscal year 2025 worth P573 million, according to prosecutors.
Only former DPWH assistant district engineer Denryl Caesar Cortuna and district engineers Manny Bulusan and Arturo Gonzales Jr. remain as Estrada’s co-accused in his plunder case.
This was the outcome of the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division’s 2-1 vote granting the prosecution’s motion as explained in a 29-page resolution dated Sept. 1 released to the media on Tuesday.
Associate Justice Gener Gito was the lone dissenting vote.

In his 32-page dissenting opinion, Gito noted that the court “is kept in the dark” as to how Bonoan would cooperate with the government, what information he would relay to the prosecution, what his testimony would be, and in which cases his testimony would be used.
“What the prosecution wants the court to do is simply accept its justification for discharging Bonoan from the information hook, line and sinker,” Gito said.

The Fifth Division resolution, however, noted that “the decision to move for the discharge of an accused is part of the Ombudsman’s prosecutorial discretion in the determination of who should be used as a state witness to bolster the successful prosecution of criminal offenses.”

“Unless made in clear violation of the Rules, this determination should be given great weight as courts do not, as a rule, have a vision of the true strength of the prosecution’s evidence until after the trial is over,” the resolution said.
Estrada’s defense counsel opposed the prosecutor’s motion, saying it would affect the senator’s defense. Cortuna, Bulusan and Gonzales likewise opposed the motion.
Prosecutors said the other accused, including Estrada, are expected to file a motion for reconsideration. /jpv

articles.title: DepEd to drop ‘active shooter reenactment’ in school safety drills
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) will no longer be conducting “reenactments” for the nationwide simultaneous school safety drill this Thursday. At the Kapihan sa Manila…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) will no longer be conducting “reenactments” for the nationwide simultaneous school safety drill this Thursday.

At the Kapihan sa Manila Prince Hotel on Wednesday, DepEd governance and operations Undersecretary Malcolm Garma explained that the drill had been postponed on August 25, due to inclement weather and concerns from medical groups regarding children’s emotional safety.

“Wala nang reenactment na mayroong active shooter or active attacker because, according to the experts, this might cause psychological trauma sa ating mga participant learners and including the teachers,” Garma said in an interview after the forum.
(There will no longer be reenactments involving an active shooter or active attacker because, according to experts, these may cause psychological trauma to participating learners and teachers.)
“What will trigger the drill are the alarms, yung distinct alarm na, once mag-sound yun, that will signal the commitment of the drills,” he added. /jpv

articles.title: Regulatory body for social media, gaming platforms pushed
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police–Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP–ACG) recommended the creation of a regulatory body for social media and gaming platforms. “It was one of our proposals…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police–Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP–ACG) recommended the creation of a regulatory body for social media and gaming platforms.

“It was one of our proposals at the top level [of government] to have this review and censorship board for all social media platforms and gaming platforms,” PNP-ACG director Maj. Gen. Wilson Asueta said at the Kapihan sa Manila Prince Hotel forum on Wednesday.
“[A board] that will really censure, monitor and tell, ‘You need to stop. This is prohibited. This is violent content,’” he added.

Asueta made this pronouncement in response to a question on whether Congress should pass a law or whether Malacañang can issue an executive order creating a body like the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) for social media platforms.
The MTRCB was formed by Presidential Decree No. 1986 issued by then-President Ferdinand E. Marcos Sr. in 1985.
“An amendment is very commendable,” Asueta said.

“And, for the meantime, an executive order, pwede i-ano ng ating SILG (Secretary of the Interior and Local Government) kasi immediate yun kaysa paggawa ng batas. But, [we’ve] proposed [a board] already in terms of legislation,” he added.
(And, for the meantime, an executive order, our SILG can push for that because that’s more immediate than passing a law. But, we’ve proposed a board already in terms of legislation.)
Regulations on social media and gaming platforms regained public interest following the fatal school shooting incidents in Tacloban City last June 22 and Zamboanga City last August 18.
Both incidents were allegedly perpetrated by teenaged students who had supposedly been exposed to violent content on social media and gaming platforms.

The PNP previously said it was studying a recommendation discussed during the Association of Southeast Asian Nation Chiefs of Police (Aseanapol) last July to adopt a measure similar to Australia’s ban on social media for users aged 16 and younger. /gsg

articles.title: They survived the flood. Their families did not.
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — When the flood came, Purna Bahadur Ghale had seconds to decide whether to run. The 43-year-old executive member of Uttargaya Rural Municipality was in Shanti Bazar when the…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — When the flood came, Purna Bahadur Ghale had seconds to decide whether to run.

The 43-year-old executive member of Uttargaya Rural Municipality was in Shanti Bazar when the Bhotekoshi river burst through settlements in Rasuwa on August 26. Someone shouted that everyone should flee.
He ran towards his home in Khalte.
Shanti Bazar is about three kilometres from the village. But by the time Ghale reached Pahirebesi, the flood had already arrived. He barely escaped with his life.
“Seconds made the difference between life and death,” he said.
Now sheltering at the holding centre set up at Shivalaya Basic School in Laharepauwa, Ghale is struggling to comprehend what happened next. Seven members of his family are missing.
“I know neither whether they are alive nor where their bodies are,” he said. “Seven of my relatives were caught in the flood.”

Ghale fled uphill into the forest and spent two days there. On the third day, Friday, a Nepali Army helicopter rescued him and flew him to Bidur in neighbouring Nuwakot. On Sunday, he made the five-hour journey back to Uttargaya.
“Ward 1 has suffered the greatest damage,” he said. “The very people who were telling others to run to safety were themselves swept away.”

The villages of Khalte, Gogane, Tiru and Karmarang have suffered extensive human and property losses. Bodies have begun appearing along the riverbanks, many so badly damaged that they are difficult to identify.

Among Ghale’s missing relatives are his 75-year-old father Subba Ghale; his 16-year-old younger son Krishna Ghale; his elder son’s 24-year-old wife Suchita; his brother Bam Bahadur’s 24-year-old wife Som Maya; their daughters, five-year-old Binusa and three-year-old Sunita; and his 10-year-old nephew Bikram Tamang.
The homes of the two brothers stood close to each other. His brother also ran a grocery shop in the village. According to Ghale, the flood reached Khalte at around 9:30am.
“I escaped the flood. When I first heard that it was coming, I called home and told everyone to run,” he said. “I rushed home to save my family, but I never made it there.”
From a safer location, he repeatedly tried calling home. At first, no one answered. Eventually, the phones went dead.
“I haven’t slept because I don’t know what happened to my family,” he said. Within moments, the settlement had been reduced to a barren riverbed.
“There was no way to get home. The roads were gone,” he said. At the time, he did not even know who among his family members had survived.
It was only after reaching Laharepauwa on Saturday that he began learning how many of his relatives had been caught in the flood.
“What can I say? I have nothing to say,” Ghale said, tears filling his eyes. “My mind is simply not working.”
Despite his own loss, Ghale was busy compiling details of those missing because of his role as a member of the rural municipality executive. By Sunday, he had counted 54 missing people.
There were 257 houses in Khalte. “Not a single house is intact,” he said. Ghale and many others in the settlement had already survived one disaster.

“We were victims of the 2015 earthquake. We survived then,” he said. “I must have gone to Singha Durbar more than a hundred times to ask the federal government to move us somewhere safer. They always said they would, but they never did.”
The families had been displaced from Gogane by the earthquake and resettled in Khalte. Now, Ghale says, the government must provide survivors with safe housing and food.
Twenty-six-year-old Ranjina Tamang is also sheltering at Shivalaya Basic School in Laharepauwa with her four-month-old son.
She survived the flood. So did four children who were with her. Ranjina was serving food at home when the flood came down the Bhotekoshi river.
She had fed her seven-year-old daughter and was getting the child ready for school. She was also preparing to eat before accompanying her daughter to Uttargaya School.
Then she heard it. A deafening roar. A wall of water carrying a dark mass of debris.
Panic set in.

She lifted her four-month-old baby onto her back. With her left hand, she held her seven-year-old son Arjan. With her right, she grabbed Smriti, her five-year-old niece. She pushed eight-year-old Nandika, another of her nieces, ahead of her, urging her to move faster.
“I ran into the forest with them,” Ranjina said. “The flood had already reached us. I was almost unconscious, but I somehow managed to save everyone.”
She feared throughout the climb that the baby strapped to her back might have fallen. “I was terrified that my son might have slipped off without me realising it,” she said.
None of them had shoes on their feet. Ranjina suffers from asthma, and running uphill made it even harder to breathe.
She first reached Gerkhu village and the following day walked for hours before arriving at Shivalaya Basic School in Rasuwa.
By then, she still had no idea who had survived and who had been swept away.
Her father, Som Bahadur Tamang, who worked at the Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project, is among those missing. Her mother, Phul Maya, has collapsed from the shock and is staying in Dandagaun in Rasuwa.
“I haven’t even been able to speak to my mother properly on the phone,” Ranjina said. “There is no electricity here, and we cannot even charge our phones.”
Three of her uncles, Man Bahadur, Mangale and Urla Tamang, are also missing. They worked as labourers at different hydropower projects under construction in Rasuwa.

Five members of her maternal uncle’s family remain out of contact as well. “I have no clothes to wear. I have asthma and no medicine. I have a cold, and my baby has a fever,” she said. “Many people here are sick.”
Tarali Maya Tamang, another resident of Khalte, is living at the same holding centre.
Her eight-year-old daughter Sunita, 12-year-old son Samir, mother-in-law Lenchon and father-in-law Mingmar Ghale are all missing.
“My children were swept away on their way to school,” she said. “My in-laws were at home when the flood suddenly came and took them.”

Her elder son Ramesh survived by running to safety. Tarali Maya herself was in Khalte when the flood struck and fled into the forest. Her husband, Temba, and elder daughter, Sushina, who were in Gogane at the time, also managed to escape to safety.
“Where do we go now? What are we going to eat? We don’t know anything,” she said, breaking down. “My family is gone. My home is gone. We have no food, no clothes, nothing.”
For Buddhi Bahadur Tamang, the disaster took his wife.

The Khalte resident, who is deaf and makes a living as a daily wage labourer, was outside his home when the flood came. He saw the water and ran. He survived, but his 43-year-old wife, Rata Kumari, could not.
His son works abroad. Because Buddhi Bahadur cannot hear, he has been unable to speak to his son on the phone. He, too, is now staying at the holding centre in Laharepauwa.
Twenty-seven-year-old Bam Bahadur Ghale lost almost everyone closest to him. His wife Som Maya and their daughters, Binusa and Sunita, were swept away.
“Now there is no one left in my family,” he said through tears. “I have nowhere to go. There is no home, no village, no relatives. We haven’t even found the bodies of our loved ones.”
He survived because he was away from home when the flood struck.
“Now I regret not being at home,” he said. “Sometimes I think that if I had gone with my family, at least I would not have to live like this, with nothing and no one.”
Survivors in the village are now struggling even with basic necessities. Many people have been crammed into a single room. New mothers have not been receiving adequate nutritious food.
Forty-two-year-old Chhegu Lama had survived the 2015 earthquake. After the disaster, he and his family had moved to the Khalte riverbed settlement. This time, he lost several members of his family.
His sister Kaisang Buti, two brothers-in-law, his father Sonam, mother Yosong Maya, younger brother Ujjen Singh Tamang and nephew Dinesh are all missing.

“After the earthquake, the government told us this was not a suitable place to live and promised to move us somewhere safer,” Lama said. “But we continued living here, and now the flood has taken everything too. There is hardly anyone left in the village. What a disaster this has been.”
He is also staying at the holding centre in Laharepauwa. The full scale of the destruction is still unclear.

According to Bishwas Nepali, a resident of nearby Kalika Rural Municipality-3 and a social activist involved in relief and rehabilitation efforts, preliminary estimates suggest that around 1,000 households across different wards of Uttargaya Rural Municipality have been affected.

“I am from this area, so we are involved in rescue, relief and rehabilitation efforts and helping in whatever way we can,” he said. “But we have not yet been able to collect complete data on the number of people affected.”

Local units and civil society groups are still compiling the figures. Many survivors escaped with nothing. “They have no clothes to wear. Children have no books or exercise copies to study with,” Nepali said.

Schools are currently being used as temporary shelters, and relief supplies have only recently begun arriving. “Representatives of the rural municipality are still occupied with rescue work and managing bodies,” he said.
According to Nepali, three areas in Uttargaya have been particularly hard hit: Mailung in ward 1, Pahirebesi in ward 4 and Khalte in ward 5.
He said government relief had yet to reach some of the affected settlements, while supplies brought by organisations and individuals were being stored and distributed through the local government.
There are currently five holding centres in the area, with students, elderly people, women and men accommodated separately.
“This arrangement may work for a short time,” Nepali said. “But if people have to stay like this for too long, health problems will emerge.” The next step, he said, must be temporary resettlement.

articles.title: Crimson sun amazes Sultan Kudarat folk
articles.summary: KORONADAL CITY — An unusually blazingly red sun greeted early risers in Tacurong City, Sultan Kudarat, on Wednesday morning, creating a striking sight against the grayish sky. Elric Batilaran, who…

blocks.text: KORONADAL CITY — An unusually blazingly red sun greeted early risers in Tacurong City, Sultan Kudarat, on Wednesday morning, creating a striking sight against the grayish sky.
Elric Batilaran, who took a photo of the sunrise, said the sun appeared unusually red as it rose over the city.
His photo showed the bright red sun above palm trees and buildings in Tacurong.
Reports said that dust, smoke, haze, and other tiny particles in the air can make red and orange colors more visible.
However, authorities have not confirmed whether haze caused the unusually red sun seen over Tacurong on Wednesday.
The sight came as haze from forest fires in Indonesia has reached some parts of the Philippines.

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) said smoke from forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, is being carried toward the Philippines by the southwest monsoon, locally known as habagat.
The haze has affected parts of Luzon and the Visayas, where several areas have recorded higher levels of fine particles in the air.
But authorities have not confirmed whether the haze from Indonesia reached Tacurong, or that the red sunrise seen in the city was a result of it.
DENR-EMB said the haze could continue to affect parts of the country from Sept. 1 to 3 as smoke from the Indonesian forest fires continues to be carried by the habagat.
The agency said rain could help clear the air by washing away smoke and other fine particles./coa

articles.title: Norway’s King Haakon VIII swears allegiance to constitution
articles.summary: OSLO — Norway’s King Haakon VIII took an oath before parliament on Tuesday, the first major institutional step of his reign, though his wife, still convalescing after a lung transplant,…

blocks.text: OSLO — Norway’s King Haakon VIII took an oath before parliament on Tuesday, the first major institutional step of his reign, though his wife, still convalescing after a lung transplant, was unable to attend.

Dressed in a ceremonial uniform, the 53-year-old Haakon, who became king when his father King Harald V died on Friday morning aged 89, swore to abide by the Scandinavian country’s constitution, under which the royals have a primarily symbolic function.
“I promise and swear that I will govern the Kingdom of Norway in accordance with its Constitution and Laws, so help me God, the almighty and omniscient,” he recited in the parliament’s main chamber.
Haakon’s wife Queen Mette-Marit, 53, was not beside her husband as she is still recovering from her June 17 transplant.

Media photographs showed her hours after the ceremony arriving at hospital in a car driven by the king himself. They showed him then leaving the facility without her and later returning to pick her up.
Are Holm, head of the Pulmonary Department at Oslo University Hospital, said in a statement from the palace that complications after a transplant are not “uncommon”.
“The queen has had complications on several occasions since the operation, including today,” Holm said.
“As a result, the queen must be kept under observation throughout the day,” he continued.
Moment of silence
The couple’s eldest daughter, Ingrid Alexandra, now crown princess at 22, attended her father’s ceremony.
She also took the oath Tuesday, but in writing at the Royal Palace.
Haakon and the members of parliament also observed a minute of silence in tribute to Harald.
Harald’s funeral will be held on September 9 at Oslo Cathedral. He will then be laid to rest in the royal mausoleum at Akershus Fortress in the Norwegian capital.
On Tuesday, thousands lined up outside the Royal Palace’s chapel where Harald is lying in state and will do so until the day before the funeral.
The king died while being treated at Oslo University Hospital for hemolytic anemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells.
He faced mounting health problems in his final years, forcing him to scale back his official schedule, but always ruled out abdicating.
Growing support
Harald, widely seen as the embodiment of an open and tolerant Norway, enjoyed massive support despite the scandals that dogged his family in the final stretch of his 35-year reign.
On Tuesday, a poll published by public broadcaster NRK showed that support for the monarchy had clearly increased following Harald’s death.

Nearly three out of four Norwegians, or 72 percent, said they supported the monarchy, a rise of eight points compared with a previous survey in May, according to the poll carried out over the weekend.
Support for the monarchy had fallen to its lowest level in February — though 60 percent were still in favour — while the royal family was mired in a series of scandals.
In particular, Mette-Marit faced scrutiny for her ties to late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
And her son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Hoiby, is currently under house arrest pending his appeal against a four-year sentence for two rape convictions.
The 29-year-old was able to visit Harald in hospital on the eve of his death and on Monday he was among those who brought the late king’s casket to the palace chapel.
He has also been granted permission to attend the funeral.

In the NRK survey, members of the royal family — of which Hoiby is not formally part — were also evaluated. Mette-Marit received one of the lowest character scores of 5.2 out of 10, compared to Haakon’s 8.8.
King Haakon and his wife will not be crowned, as Norway abolished coronations in 1908.
But, like his father and grandfather before him, Haakon could opt for a consecration ceremony at Trondheim Cathedral, where Norwegian monarchs were crowned between 1814 and 1906. /dl

articles.title: PNP heightens police visibility during ‘ber’ months
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) has ordered increased police visibility in areas expected to draw larger crowds as the country enters the “ber” months. According to PNP…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) has ordered increased police visibility in areas expected to draw larger crowds as the country enters the “ber” months.

According to PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., regional and city police offices are directed to strengthen police visibility, patrols and monitoring in commercial establishments, transport terminals, markets and other public places where people are expected to converge.
He also ordered PNP personnel to strengthen presence in crime-prone areas across the country.
The PNP chief said police units would coordinate closely with local authorities and other stakeholders to address emerging security concerns.
“Our priority is to prevent crimes before they happen and ensure a safe and peaceful holiday season,” Nartatez said in a press release on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, Nartatez urged the public to secure their belongings, avoid sharing real-time locations online and immediately report suspicious activities to authorities to prevent crimes, such as theft, robbery, and scams.
He pointed out that keeping communities safe during the holiday season would require cooperation between the police and the public. Rendell Ivan Manuel, INQUIRER.net trainee /jpv

articles.title: Senate impeachment court removes 'abogadong walang alam' describing Poa off the record
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has struck down the "abogadong walang alam" (a lawyer who knows nothing) remark of private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. from Senate records when he questioned Vice…

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 11:24am

The Senate impeachment court has struck down the "abogadong walang alam" (a lawyer who knows nothing) remark of private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. from Senate records when he questioned Vice President Sara Duterte's counsel Michael Poa about his knowledge on confidential fund spending at the Department of Education (DepEd).
This developed after defense team lead counsel Sheila Sison called out Tolosa's statement as a "rhetoric to provide drama" during Day 21 of Duterte's impeachment trial.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said such description of Tolosa is not fitting to describe a fellow lawyer.
"The chair orders to strike abogadong walang alam off the records. The chair finds it discourteous, to say the least," Escudero said.

Tolosa said his comments were not meant to disparage Poa and were based on latter's previous testimony before a House inquiry that "he knew totally nothing" about DepEd's confidential fund disbursements.
"I offended you, I am sorry. I wasn't my intention," Tolosa said.

Poa bowed out as spokesperson of the defense panel's spokesperson when he was called by the prosecution to testify in the impeachment trial regarding the use of confidential funds in the DepEd during Duterte's tenure as the agency's secretary. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Death toll from Luis, Maymay, Neneng, Habagat now at 39 -- OCD
articles.summary: The death toll from the combined effects of tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng as well as the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat has risen to 39, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 11:24am
The death toll from the combined effects of tropical cyclones Luis, Maymay, and Neneng as well as the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat has risen to 39, the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) said Wednesday.
In its report as of 6 a.m., the OCD said Benguet recorded the highest number of fatalities at 15, including 10 in Baguio City, two in La Trinidad, and three in Atok, all due to landslides.
Rizal and Batangas each recorded four deaths.
In Rizal, two people died due to a rockslide in Rodriguez, one due to a fallen tree in Antipolo, and one due to drowning in Binangonan.
In Batangas, one death each was recorded in Batangas City due to drowning, Lipa due to electrocution, Santa Teresita due to a landslide, and Mabini due to drowning.
Zambales recorded three deaths, including two from a landslide in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone on the Morong, Bataan side as well as one in Olongapo City.
Caloocan also recorded three deaths, all due to drowning.
Two deaths each were reported in Pampanga, Quezon, and Occidental Mindoro, while La Union, Pangasinan, Oriental Mindoro and Negros Occidental each recorded one fatality.
The OCD also reported 20 injured persons and three people still missing.
Affected population

A total of 9.4 million people or 2.7 million families were affected by the weather disturbances in Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, Bicol, Western Visayas, Calabarzon, Cordillera Administrative Region, Metro Manila, and Mimaropa.
A total of 71,364 people or 20,279 families were staying inside 968 evacuation centers as flooding was reported in 711 areas.
The OCD reported 3,900 damaged houses — 3,400 partially and 538 totally.
Infrastructure damage has reached ₱6.27 billion, while agricultural damage was placed at ₱2.84 billion, according to the OCD.

articles.title: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty in 2nd national security case
articles.summary: Prominent Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty Wednesday to conspiracy to collude with foreign forces to endanger national security under a Beijing-imposed law that has…

image.caption: Supporters of Joshua Wong hold signs during a press event to support the pro-democracy activist in Taipei, Taiwan, Wednesday. Wong pleaded guilty to a national security charge in Hong Kong. (Chiang Ying-ying/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

Prominent Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty Wednesday to conspiracy to collude with foreign forces to endanger national security under a Beijing-imposed law that has effectively stifled the city's once-thriving pro-democracy movement.
Wong is already serving a previous sentence that was due to end in January

It was the second prosecution of Wong, a former student leader in the pro-democracy movement and one of its most recognizable faces, under the national security law introduced in Hong Kong in 2020 to quell massive anti-government protests that rocked the city the year before.
Wong, who wore a blue shirt, appeared thinner as he entered his plea.

Before the hearing, a supporter shouted "hang in there" to Wong. His friend Louis Lee said Wong read books, studied, learned guitar and exercised in prison, exploring new hobbies and new things behind bars. He said he hoped to see Wong outside prison as soon as possible.
"I believe he and I, or friends outside, we will do our best in our own roles and continue to work hard in our fields," he said.
Current sentence due to end in January

Wong is expected to be sentenced later. The offence is punishable by a prison term of three to 10 years, or up to life imprisonment if the offence is deemed to be "of a grave nature." Pleading guilty could typically result in a reduced sentence.
He was already serving a prison term of four years and eight months after entering a guilty plea in a separate national security case linked to an unofficial political primary.
Before the arrest for the collusion-related offense in June 2025, Wong had been expected to be freed next January.

Critics say Wong's case showed the authorities' determination to silence prominent dissidents, chilling civic activism. But to Beijing, Wong is an anti-China figure who supports Hong Kong independence, a red line for authorities.
Rose to prominence as student activist

Wong, 29, was accused of conspiring with fellow activist Nathan Law and others to ask foreign countries, or institutions, organizations, or individuals outside China to impose sanctions, blockades or engage in other hostile actions against Hong Kong or China from July 1-Nov. 23, 2020.

In 2012, Wong rose to prominence as a high school student leading protests against the introduction of national education in Hong Kong schools. His fame spread later as a student leader of the 2014 Occupy Movement.
Wong co-founded a political party, "Demosisto," in 2016 with fellow young activists, including Law, who became the city's youngest lawmaker that same year.

items: Pro-democracy activist Nathan Law is on China's wanted list. Here's why

blocks.text: During the leaderless 2019 protests, Wong helped seek overseas support for the democracy movement, including from the U.S. But Beijing criticized his actions, saying he "begged for interference" by foreign countries.
Demosisto disbanded when Beijing imposed the security law in 2020, which authorities said was necessary for the city's stability.
Many other leading activists were also jailed under the same law, including former media tycoon Jimmy Lai. Some activists fled to other democratic countries, including the U.S. and the U.K.

Hong Kong authorities separately offered rewards of one million Hong Kong dollars ($176,000 Cdn) for information leading to the arrests of Law, who moved to Britain, and other overseas-based activists.

HONG KONG – Prominent Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty on Wednesday< September 2, to a charge of collusion with foreign entities, a national security crime that carries a maximum sentence of life in prison.

Wong, 29, rose to international prominence as a teenage democracy activist in Hong Kong, one of a group of youngsters whose protest efforts have now effectively been outlawed by a sweeping National Security Law that Beijing imposed on the Asian financial hub in 2020.

Wearing a dark blue shirt and black-rimmed glasses, Wong waved and nodded to people from the court’s dock, inhaling deeply at times, before pleading guilty to a government-approved national security judge at Hong Kong’s High Court in the district of Admiralty.
Several Western diplomats attended the hearing.

The prosecution highlighted what it said was an international media and political campaign by Demosisto, a now-disbanded political party that once backed a referendum on Hong Kong’s sovereignty and counted Wong as one of its leaders, that sought to bring sanctions on Hong Kong and China in 2019 and 2020.

Wong is already in jail serving an existing sentence on an earlier national security charge of conspiracy to commit subversion after he was among a group of democratic activists who participated in an unofficial primary election in 2020. His current sentence is scheduled to end next year.

A charge sheet seen earlier by Reuters accused Wong of having conspired with exiled activist Nathan Law and others to ask foreign countries, institutions, organizations, or individuals outside China to impose sanctions or blockades.
Such actions against Hong Kong or China, along with other hostile activities targeting them, took place in 2020, between July 1 and November 23, it added.
Wong’s case and others are being closely watched by international human rights groups and some Western countries tracking the implementation of the National Security Law.
His case comes after two other activists were found guilty of inciting subversion last month after they used the phrase “end one-party dictatorship” in their political activities.
Lee Cheuk-yan, ‌69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, were part of a group known for organizing annual vigils marking Beijing’s 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown on pro-democracy protesters.
Hong Kong’s National Security Law was passed on June 30, 2020, in part as a response to months of sometimes-violent pro-democracy protests that roiled the city in 2019.

While international human rights groups and Western countries criticized the law as excessive given the high degree of autonomy Hong Kong was promised following its handover from British to Chinese rule in 1997, Hong Kong and Chinese officials said it was vital to restore stability. – Rappler.com
